The dashed lines show the hidden bottom-face edges BA, AD and the vertical edge AE. Reasoning: Pyramid ABCH can take triangle ABC as the base, and point H as the apex. Triangle ABC is located within the prism bottom face ABCD, and it is half of rectangle ABCD, so area(ABC) = 1/2 area(ABCD). Point H is on the top face, and its perpendicular distance to the bottom-face plane ABC equals the height of the entire rectangular prism. Therefore Volume(ABCH) = (1/3) * area(ABC) * height = (1/3) * (1/2 area(ABCD)) * height = 1/6 * Volume(ABCDEFGH). Given Volume(ABCH)=20, so Volume(ABCDEFGH)=6*20=120.

raw_record.question_text:

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a right rectangular prism with bottom face ABCD and top face EFGH, with vertical pairs A-E, B-F, C-G, D-H. The pyramid ABCH has triangular base ABC lying in the bottom rectangular face. Since ABC is half of the rectangular base ABCD, its area is half the base area of the prism. The apex H is on the top face, so its perpendicular height to plane ABC is the same as the prism height. Therefore Volume(ABCH) = (1/3)(1/2 base area)(height) = 1/6 of the prism volume. Use the text fact Volume(ABCH)=20, so prism volume = 6*20 = 120.
